findings.title: Web dashboard's primary interactions are mouse-only (runner cards, sortable headers, table rows)
evidence: server/web/app.js:392 - runner panels are `<div class="runner ..." data-runner="...">`; opening the live view is bound to a click only
server/web/app.js:1734 - `document.addEventListener("click", (e) => {...})` is the single interaction entry point; app.js:1743 dispatches [data-runner],[data-detail],[data-focus], etc.
server/web/app.js:862 - sortable `<th class="sortable">` are re-rendered from the click handler (app.js:1735-1741) with no keyboard/Enter/Space path
server/web/app.js:880 - history rows `<tr data-detail="...">` and app.js:928 fleet rows are clickable only
server/web/style.css:58 `.runner{...cursor:pointer}`, style.css:110 `tbody tr{cursor:pointer}`, style.css:194 `th.sortable{cursor:pointer}`
server/web - grep for `tabindex`/`role=`/`keydown` on these elements returns nothing; only two global keydown listeners exist (app.js:1716, app.js:1825) and neither covers them
findings.impact: Keyboard-only and assistive-technology users cannot open a runner's live view, sort the history table, or open a run's detail — core tasks in the control plane.
findings.recommendation: Render the clickable panels/rows/headers as real `<button>`/`<a>` or add tabindex=0 + role=button/row and an Enter/Space keydown handler; add aria-sort to the sorted `<th>`.

findings.title: Modal dialog has no dialog semantics, no focus trap, and no focus restore
evidence:
server/web/index.html:146 - `
` has no role="dialog" / aria-modal / aria-labelledby
server/web/app.js:1708-1712 - `openModal()` sets innerHTML, adds `.show`, and focuses only the first input; the rest of the page stays focusable
server/web/app.js:1714 - `closeModal()` only removes the class; focus is not returned to the element that opened it
server/web/app.js:1724 - backdrop click closes; Escape is handled at app.js:1717 but Tab is not trapped
findings.impact: Screen-reader users are not told a dialog opened, and Tab moves focus behind the overlay (start/stop/reboot/shutdown controls); after closing, keyboard focus is lost, which is disorienting for destructive actions that are confirm-gated.
findings.recommendation: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby to #modalbox, trap Tab within the modal while open, and restore focus to the invoking control on close.

findings.title: No ARIA anywhere in the web dashboard; tab strip and live SSE updates are not exposed to assistive tech
evidence: server/web - grep for `aria-*` / `role=` / `aria-live` across app.js, index.html, style.css returns no matches
server/web/index.html:27-34 - the six tabs are plain `<button data-tab=...>` with no role="tablist"/role="tab"/aria-selected; the panes are `<section id="tab-*" class="tabpane">`
server/web/app.js:1765-1772 - tab switching only toggles the `active` class / display, so no selected-state or panel linkage is announced
server/web/app.js:280-288 - live telemetry/gauges and phase updates mutate the DOM on each SSE batch with no aria-live region to announce them
findings.impact: Assistive-technology users get no indication of which tab is selected and no announcement of live run/telemetry changes — a core function of the live fleet view.
findings.recommendation: Add tablist/tab/tabpanel roles with aria-selected and roving tabindex, and mark the live summary/console regions aria-live="polite" (console log off or aria-live="off").

findings.title: Canvas charts have no accessible alternative and their tooltips are pointer-only
evidence: server/web/index.html:93 - `<canvas id="trendChart" height="360"></canvas>` with no role="img"/aria-label and no text fallback
server/web/app.js:1166-1187 - `attachHover()` reads values only from `mousemove` and hides on `mouseleave`; there is no keyboard/touch equivalent
server/web/app.js:1118-1119 - drawChart stores `cv._chart` and attaches hover; the plotted points are never emitted as text/table
findings.impact: The Trends, Compare and run-detail charts are opaque to screen readers and to keyboard users; the same numbers are only reachable by hovering with a mouse.
findings.recommendation: Give each canvas role="img" with an aria-label summarising the series, and provide an accessible data table or a focusable legend listing the values (chartLegendHTML already computes the range).

findings.title: Tk GUI suppresses the keyboard focus indicator and has no keyboard accelerators
evidence: bench/gui.py:255-256 - TButton style sets `borderwidth=0, focusthickness=0`, removing the focus ring
bench/gui.py:276 - TCheckbutton style sets `focuscolor=CARD`, so a focused checkbox is visually identical to an unfocused one
bench/gui.py:331 - the only `bind()` found is `<<ComboboxSelected>>`; there are no `<Key>` accelerators or menu keyboard bindings anywhere in gui.py (grep)
findings.impact: Keyboard users cannot see which widget has focus in the Tk dashboard, making Tab-based operation unreliable, and there are no shortcuts for start/stop/collect on the core operator surface.
findings.recommendation: Remove `focusthickness=0` and set a visible `focuscolor` (e.g. ACCENT); add keyboard accelerators for start/stop/collect.

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion or prefers-color-scheme support; theme is fixed dark
evidence: server/web/style.css:73-75 - `@keyframes pulse{...}` is applied to `.statusp.busy` (style.css:73) and `.rtabs .rtab.live .dot` (style.css:220) with no way to disable it
server/web/style.css:1-6 - `:root` hard-codes the dark palette (--bg:#0f1218, --text:#dce3ee, ...) with no light variant
server/web - grep for `prefers-reduced-motion` / `prefers-color-scheme` across the web assets returns no matches
findings.impact: Users who set 'reduce motion' at the OS level still get the perpetually pulsing busy/live indicators (WCAG 2.3.3); users who rely on a light theme cannot adapt the always-dark dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to stop the pulse/transition animations, and honour `prefers-color-scheme` (or provide a theme toggle) for a light palette.

findings.title: Offline runner cards dimmed with opacity .55 drops muted metadata below AA contrast
evidence: server/web/style.css:65 - `.runner.off{opacity:.55}`
server/web/style.css:2,63 - the dimmed metadata uses `--muted:#8592a6` (`.runner .rrow .rk` and `.rrv`)
computed: #8592a6 composited at 55% over the #0f1218 page background is ~#505866, a contrast ratio of ~2.6:1 (below the 4.5:1 AA minimum)
findings.impact: The 'last run' / device metadata on offline runners (still informational — what the box last achieved) becomes hard to read for low-vision users.
findings.recommendation: Dim with a lighter overlay/opacity (or a lighter muted token) so dimmed text stays >=4.5:1, or keep offline state as a badge rather than reducing overall opacity.

findings.title: No accessibility or visual-regression tooling or tests for any UI surface
evidence: tests/test_dashboards.py:99-105 - the web 'live view' tests are source-level string matches; the docstring states 'the suite has no browser'
tests/test_dashboards.py:106-132 - assertions check for identifiers like `data-rtab=` in app.js, not rendered behaviour or a11y
repo grep (case-insensitive) for axe|pa11y|lighthouse|playwright|cypress|storybook|WCAG|a11y returns no test/config evidence in the repository
findings.impact: There is no automated guard against keyboard/ARIA/contrast regressions in the GUI, TUI or web dashboard; the a11y gaps above can silently worsen.
findings.recommendation: Add a browser-based check (Playwright + axe-core) over the served dashboard, assert tab/focus/keyboard behaviour, and add a Lighthouse/axe CI job; include reduced-motion and a keyboard-only smoke run.
